chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ali ibn Asbat, from a man from our companions who is called Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man entered upon him and gave him thirty dinars to perform Hajj on behalf of Ismail. He did not leave out anything from Umrah to Hajj except that he stipulated for him, until he stipulated for him that he should walk in Wadi Muhassir. Then he said, 'O this man, if you do this, then for Ismail there will be a Hajj for what he spent from his wealth, and for you there will be nine [Hajjs] for what you exhausted of your body.'

key_terms.دِينَاراً: Dinar (a gold coin used as currency)
key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّرٍ: Wadi Muhassir (a valley near Mecca where pilgrims walk due to fear of traffic/crowds, a specific ritual stipulation)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in reward between the person who pays for Hajj and the one who performs it physically?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of proportional reward distribution in *Hajj al-Badal* (Hajj on behalf of another), distinguishing between the donor's financial contribution and the performer's physical labor. By stipulating the specific act of walking in Wadi Muhassir, the Imam highlights that ritual compliance and effort are integral to the validity of the proxy performance. This narrative underscores the theological view that spiritual merit is shared according to the distinct roles of wealth and bodily exertion in fulfilling religious obligations.
